# Welcome {-}

`evalpheno` brings together temperature-driven phenology models, parameter
calibration, and simulations of variation among individual buds. This guide
takes you from your first model to more detailed calibration and bud-population
workflows.

## Read the guide {-}

1. [Getting started](getting-started.html): construct a model, prepare weather
   data, predict bloom dates, and fit model parameters.
2. [Model structures and submodels](model-structures-and-submodels.html): choose
   how chill and heat accumulation interact and inspect their parameters.
3. [Model calibration](model-calibration_special-cases.html): explore
   cross-validation, successive stages, and calibration across cultivars.
4. [Bud populations](bud-population.html): simulate variation among buds and
   their responses to cutting and forcing experiments.

Use the chapter sidebar to move through the guide, the contents panel to find
sections within a chapter, or the search box to find a topic across chapters.

## Install evalpheno {-}

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("larscaspersen/eval_phenoflex")
```

The examples use R packages such as `chillR`, `DEoptim`, and `ggplot2`. Install
the package's suggested dependencies to run all examples:

```{r install-examples, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github("larscaspersen/eval_phenoflex", dependencies = TRUE)
```

## About the examples {-}

The guide uses the package's bundled weather data. Synthetic phenology dates
and short optimizer runs illustrate the interfaces; use your own observations
and suitable calibration settings for research applications.

The chapters are built from the package vignettes, so the online guide and the
installed package documentation share the same source.

Visit the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/larscaspersen/eval_phenoflex)
for source code, issues, and development updates.
